# Auto-generated rule: NUL-byte corruption needs a byte-level pre-commit gate; POSIX tr|cmp is the only portable detector

NUL bytes written into a source file survive BOTH vitest and eslint (parsers stop at the first token error only if the NUL breaks syntax; often it does not), so the only cheap mechanical catch is a byte-level gate over staged text files. The detector must be 'LC_ALL=C tr -d \000 < f | cmp -s - f' — 'grep -P' is GNU-only and '$'\''\x00'\''' is a bashism dash cannot parse; worse, 'grep -q "$(printf \000)"' silently matches everything because command substitution strips NUL, degrading the gate to a no-op that still exits 0.

## Evidence
2026-07-27 P1: extracted-block dry-run in a tmp git repo — real POSIX block exits 1 on a staged corrupt .mjs and 0 on clean files; the command-substitution variant exits 0 on the SAME corrupt file (fake-regression proof). Wired as stage 2 of .husky/pre-commit with marker-delimited block executed verbatim by tests/husky/pre-commit-nul-byte-guard.test.mjs (4 tests green).
